title: Restricting an adjunction along fully faithful functors, with its unit and counit
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal C',\mathcal D'$ be categories in arbitrary universes, with fully faithful functors $i:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ and $j:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ (the induced maps on every Hom set are bijections). Let $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$, $F':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$ and $G':\mathcal D'\to\mathcal C'$ be functors. Suppose $F'\dashv G'$ has natural Hom bijections $\Phi'$, unit $\eta'$ and counit $\varepsilon'$, and there are natural isomorphisms $b:jF\xrightarrow{\sim}F'i$ and $c:iH\xrightarrow{\sim}G'j$.

Then the composite bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D}(FM,K)\xrightarrow{j}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D'}(jFM,jK)\xrightarrow{-\circ b_M^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal D'}(F'iM,jK)\xrightarrow{\Phi'}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C'}(iM,G'jK)\xrightarrow{c_K^{-1}\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C'}(iM,iHK)\xrightarrow{i^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(M,HK)$$
is natural in both variables and defines an adjunction $F\dashv H$. Here $i^{-1}$ denotes the inverse of the map on Hom sets, not an inverse functor. Its unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ satisfy both triangle identities and
$$i(\eta_M)=c_{FM}^{-1}\circ G'(b_M^{-1})\circ\eta'_{iM},\qquad j(\varepsilon_K)=\varepsilon'_{jK}\circ F'(c_K)\circ b_{HK}.$$
Composition is read right to left. Adjunction, natural Hom bijections, unit and counit have the conventions of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection].
